Bluenoroff is tied to bank heists, including an attempted $851 million SWIFT theft, and the groups are said to have stolen cryptocurrency from exchanges. 1f19d02f56c7877c675714f6f03bbd5ba1e929aa.summary: BleepingComputer article on Hadooken, a new Linux malware that targets Oracle WebLogic servers, citing Aqua Security researchers. The malware drops a cryptominer and the Tsunami DDoS botnet, sets up cron jobs, and wipes system logs. Static analysis linked it to the RHOMBUS and NoEscape ransomware families, though no ransomware modules were seen in the observed attacks. A PowerShell script on one delivery server downloaded Mallox ransomware for Windows. The researchers counted more than 230,000 WebLogic servers on the public web.

Intrusions began with broad port scanning, password guessing on exposed management interfaces and exploitation of vulnerabilities, often routed through compromised relay servers. The group kept access through backdoors, VPN accounts lacking multi-factor authentication and jump-host targeting, removed traces, stole data and account credentials, and destroyed network equipment. 1f7487abb5b7f175e96b43fdd08d2d151e16bc4e.summary: A technical tutorial, not a report on an observed threat. It explains how to load a shared library into a running Linux process with the GDB debugger, using process attachment. The sample library starts a reverse shell that calls back to a listener at a fixed interval. The author also covers detection artifacts: process listings, files on disk, and service disruption. Tools mentioned include GDB, CobaltStrike (as training inspiration) and pcapknock (used during the author's work). No actors, CVEs, dates, sectors or countries are named.

1fa5348b18acafb16216f2b891b00066ddc8e5fd.summary: Intezer researchers describe SysJoker, a C++ backdoor that targets Windows, Linux and macOS and is undetected on VirusTotal at the time of writing. The Windows variant uses a DLL dropper and PowerShell. All variants fetch C2 server addresses from a hardcoded Google Drive file, collect system data, and persist via a Run registry key, a cron job or a LaunchAgent. The malware was first seen in December 2021 and the article was published January 11, 2022.
